waves.name: Sequenced batch job
waves.rationale: One job, three programs, no shared dataset. The seed puts the whole system in one family, and that is sound: there is no second entry point to sequence against, no data hub, no cycle and no computed call. The programs are empty (GOBACK only), so the family test 'writes nothing shared' holds by absence of code, not by proof of behavior. The one constraint is the step order in SEQJOB, which lives only in JCL file order. It can be deployed and rolled back as one job, and its boundary is testable by step order and return codes.
waves.unblocks: Nothing else in this tree depends on it. It is the whole system, so it works as the proof of the toolchain, and it is a chore beyond that until the real program bodies and the scheduler export arrive.
